doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: How he joined the Woody Herman band
summary: Nat Pierce and Jake Hanna heard him at a club and he joined Woody Herman, who was generous about his young arranger's writing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It’s fairly profound. Did you have a passion to play and tour with a big band? Or was that one of the things that came up and you said, and speaking of Woody Herman, “Well yeah, I’ll try that. I need a gig.”

Well how I joined Woody is that a great pianist/arranger Nat Pierce and the great drummer, they were both with Woody back in the heyday ‘60s I mean — Jake Hanna and Nat came down to hear me play at a club and it was the end of my last year and the semester and I needed a way to extend my visa and here was an opportunity. So they heard me and heard I was an arranger and I went out with Woody. So that was that.

Most of the guys, you could correct me if I’m wrong, but most of the band, as time went by, became quite a bit younger than Woody. And did he take — embrace the opportunity to be introduced to music that he might not have normally considered for his band?
Yeah I guess so. I mean considering some of the crap I wrote and that he was open to. I mean he was a very generous guy with that and he saw something in this kid, I don’t know.
